method: Self-contained data audit of the exact CSV pinned as this KPI's own dataset_fixture_sha256 (feedback/v1/external_data/openpoly_benchmark/raw/final_polymer_properties_fromliterature.csv, sha256 verified to match byte-for-byte). The CSV carries a per-polymer physical decomposition never before audited: 'Dielectric Constant Total', 'Dielectric Constant Electronic', 'Dielectric Constant Ionic' (295/295 rows all three present) plus an independent 'Refractive Index' column (148/741 rows). Four pre-registered physical/definitional checks: R1 ionic>=0 (Frohlich 1949 Ch.2, non-negative polarization-mechanism contributions); R2 electronic>=1 (Maxwell eps_inf=n^2, n>=1 by definition of phase velocity, same citation W2 used for RadonPy); R3 total==electronic+ionic within 0.011 tolerance (Clausius-Mossotti additive decomposition, cited verbatim in the TARGET KPI's own theory field; tolerance = 0.01 physical rounding of independently-2-decimal-rounded source fields + float-repr epsilon); R4 refractive_index>=1 (Lorentz-Lorenz, identical citation basis W2 already used for RadonPy's refractive-index axis). Positive control: 12 defects planted on a deep copy of the real rows (3 per rule, targeted at rows that were clean in the real data), re-running the identical, unmodified audit() function against the corrupted copy and confirming every planted defect is caught by its targeted rule (R1/R2 single-field mutations also mechanically cross-trigger R3 additivity for the same rows, which is physically correct, not double-counting -- verified per-defect by row name, not merely by rule-level counts). Two-replay: audit() re-run twice on the identical real-data input, byte-identical JSON confirmed.
objective: Test whether the OpenPoly-derived ground-truth dielectric-constant labels feeding openpoly-dielectric-constant-ml-baseline-kpi.v1.json (295 polymers, RandomForest scaffold-safe holdout MAE=0.4040 vs NULL 0.7027, LOSO-CV R2=+0.659, status STANDS) are physically admissible, using the SAME Frohlich(1949)/Maxwell/Lorentz-Lorenz physical-bound methodology this module's own C8/W2 fires already used to REFUTE the sibling RadonPy dielectric corpora, applied here to OpenPoly for the first time.

positive_control.how_planted: See positive_control.planted_defects[] below for the exact row name, field, before-value and after-value of each of the 12 mutations, produced by corrupt_rows() in compute_openpoly_dielectric_admissibility.py (deterministic, seed-free -- operates on the first N rows with each field present, not randomly sampled).

pre_registered_refute_criterion: If >=1 row violates R1 (ionic>=0), R2 (electronic>=1), R3 (total==electronic+ionic within 0.011), or R4 (refractive_index>=1) on the REAL data, the KPI's ground-truth dielectric labels are physically inadmissible and the claim is REFUTED. If 0 rows violate all four on real data AND the positive control (12 planted defects, 3 per rule) is fully detected on the corrupted copy, the claim SURVIVES this attack.
